dod_intent_evidence: No SBIR, no DoD contract record, and no program-office, warfighter or service-branch language anywhere in the pack. Their about page lists "Defense & Aerospace" as one of six addressable verticals alongside Medical, Mobility and Energy, and the only defense-adjacent fact is Lockheed Martin participating in the seed round per the Origin Ventures LinkedIn post — investor membership, which the gate explicitly does not accept.
score_evidence: "INTALUS integrates ceramics into metal to create engineered material architectures for demanding applications across a wide range of industries" → horizontal materials supplier, not a defense product company
"OEMs and manufacturers trust INTALUS to perform in demanding environments" → the customer is an OEM, not a government program; any DoD exposure is several tiers of subcontract away

Proven use cases are listed as Defense & Aerospace, Space Systems, Industrial & Maritime, Medical, Energy & Nuclear, Mobility → defense is one sixth of an addressable-market list, with no named customer, contract or award
Their own newest news item is "INTALUS moves into production with new facility at Purdue's HAMTC... for government and industrial use" — a facility announcement, not a defense contract
Funding news ("$11M Seed", "raised an additional $20M... alongside Lockheed Martin and Scout Ventures") is the sole defense signal, and it is investor-side
what_they_do: An Indiana advanced-materials startup whose patented Targeted Phase Infusion process fuses ceramic into finished metal parts for wear, corrosion and thermal resistance without a surface coating.
